cs.t: A typewriter is extreme. In school I used an AlphaSmart ( https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AlphaSmart , because my handwriting sucked). A laptop without internet would also work.
cs.th: College instructor turns to typewriters to curb AI-written work

cs.t: An old AlphaSmart can be picked up for a few hundred dollars on eBay. Kind of a clever distraction-free text editor. I picked up a couple a few years ago. Pretty clever in that, one way it transfers files. You connect the device via USB to a functional computer and ready an empty document in your text-editor of choice. Push a button on the device and it sends the internal text as though from a USB keyboard to your computer: speed-typing [1]. [1]  https://youtu.be/xXuRZbq8-0s?si=AbLZ4DcnhpkUYANG&t=93

I have an AlphaSmart. I never really got on with it and will probably sell it soon. I quite like the approach proposed here: can re-use your own hardware, bring your own monitor (I hated the AlphaSmart's screen), even hack around a bit from bash.
